title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
summary:
HIV-associated lymphoma is common where HIV is common and rare in the cohorts that define lymphoma genomics. This cohort addresses that gap directly: 70 cases with whole genome sequencing on 66, RNA sequencing on 55 and microRNA on 60, of which 34 patients are recorded as Black or African American and 18 as white.
Clinical annotation is better than the cohort size suggests. Prior treatment is recorded for 81%, ECOG performance status for 71%, treatment outcome for 46%, and named regimens including CHOP-21, COM and COP for 24%.
one_liner: 70 diffuse large B-cell lymphomas from an HIV-enriched cohort, half Black or African American, with whole genome sequencing on 66 and named chemotherapy regimens on a quarter.

useful_for.question: How does the genomic landscape of HIV-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma differ from that of lymphoma in immunocompetent patients?
useful_for.rationale: Whole genome sequencing on 66 cases from an HIV-enriched population, contrastable with the many DLBCL cohorts derived from largely HIV-negative populations. Whole genome rather than exome makes structural and viral-integration analysis possible.
useful_for.statistical_note: 70 cases supports description of recurrent alterations but not genome-wide discovery at conventional significance thresholds.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Does immune status shape the tumor transcriptome in lymphoma?
useful_for.rationale: RNA sequencing on 55 cases with ECOG performance status on 71% allows transcriptional programs to be related to a clinical proxy for host status.
useful_for.statistical_note: ECOG is a crude proxy for immune competence; CD4 count would be far better and is not available in these records.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: What are the outcomes of HIV-associated DLBCL treated with standard regimens?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status is informative for 76% of cases, follow-up is derivable for 57 of 70 with a median of 11.3 months extending to 99.6, and 24% carry a named regimen.
useful_for.statistical_note: 53 cases with informative vital status gives wide confidence intervals; median follow-up of 11.3 months is short for lymphoma outcomes.

analysis_examples.question: Is performance status associated with response to chemoradiation, and which agents were actually given?
analysis_examples.problem: Disease-status codes and true response categories are easy to mix into one misleading outcome.
analysis_examples.lesson: Validate the response field, collapse repeated records, and state what the observational result cannot prove.
analysis_examples.figure: Two panels: a bar chart of how many cases carry each response label against how many carry none, and box plots of ECOG performance status for responders against progressors.
